items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: The laws of physics are CPT-symmetric, yet laboratory quantum mechanics prepares the past and only samples the future. This working paper distinguishes five levels of taking the symmetry seriously — symmetric laws with the open future left implicit, a two-boundary description, symmetric processes, a nontrivial final boundary, and laboratory access to it — places published views and experiments on them, and states what each predicts for a final-boundary test, in which an engineered terminal acts on a flag and an entangled partner is read on every trial. Exact results: an open future propagates backward through any physical channel; a terminal can only transfer, never manufacture, final-side contrast, giving lambda = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k T_f) in a swap model, the mirror of a reset; a clamp of budget A needs an energy of at least k T_f ln A in some branch; under free local control any every-trial final condition signals, with visibility equal to the clamp strength. Under stated transfer models a null reads as a lower bound on a swap-equivalent final temperature (Partridge: above 3.5e7 K for escaping microwaves; planned qubit tests: about 27 K and 360 K). The paper audits transport to the future, specifies what any physical source of a final condition must supply, and finds that no named candidate meets the specification. CPT motivates the reversed-resource question; channel duality bounds its possible transfer; laboratory access remains an additional physical hypothesis, decided only by experiment. No new experimental result is reported. Drafted with AI assistance and revised after AI-assisted reviews; responsibility rests with the author.

items.summary: We develop a rigorous asymptotic-statistical theory for the inference of stochastic-belief extended realities (SBxRs), the path-space probabilistic objects introduced in [1] for the modelling of perceptual experience in extended-reality systems. Given n independent percept trajectories drawn from an SBxR with an unknown parameter θ0 ∈ Θ ⊂ Rd and a known modality-weight structure, we construct an importance-weighted plug-in estimator ˆgn of the aggregated Fisher–Rao metric g, prove its strong consistency and asymptotic normality under standard mixing-and-moment conditions on the per-modality Itˆo diffusions, and establish operator-norm concentration via matrix Bernstein. The aggregated maximum-likelihood estimator ˆθn is shown to be consistent and asymptotically efficient with limiting covariance g(θ0)−1, and the plug-in estimator ˆgn(ˆθn) inherits a delta-method-style central limit theorem. We then address the joint identifiability of the aggregation exponent p ∈ (1,∞] from the Lp-Fisher–Rao Finsler family of [4], proving that p is qualitatively identifiable under a non-collinearity condition on the per-modality Fisher matrices but that the Fisher information for p saturates as p → ∞, with a closed-form per-direction saturation point p⋆(ξ) = 1/ log(r1(ξ)/r2(ξ)) in terms of the typical ratio of largest to second-largest weighted per-modality Fisher contributions. The estimator ˆpK achieves the parametric rate K−1/2 uniformly on a bounded interval [1, peff ] determined by this saturation point but degrades to non-parametric rates beyond it. We provide a Le Cam two-point minimax lower bound matching the upper bound up to constants, extend the framework to non-Gaussian percept processes (jump-diffusions via Jacod–Shiryaev; fractional-Brownian percepts via Shimizu– Nakajima 2024), and prove the validity of an i.i.d. path-bootstrap. A JAX implementation and eight numerical experiments validate the theory on the trichromatic-color worked example of [1] and on synthetic non-Gaussian percept models. items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. Kaggle. https://doi.org/10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/195341 Official source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`).

items.summary: Replication package for the journal article on attributing LLM-paraphrased source code to the model that produced it, in the setting where someone has an LLM rewrite code that another person wrote so that it no longer looks copied. Contents: the corpus of 144,958 paraphrase pairs (22,053 human-written files in Python, C, C++, Java, C#, Go and PHP, rewritten by Gemini 3 Flash, GPT 5 Nano, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen 3 Coder 30B, DeepSeek V3.2, Grok 4 Fast and Devstral 2512 under the paraphrasing instruction of Park et al., 2025), the deterministic fold assignment, the 105-feature matrix, the cross-prompt corpus (the same 1,050 files rewritten under two further instructions), 2,400 human revisions of source files from MIT-licensed repositories (the negative set of the paired detection experiment), the out-of-fold outputs of every view and baseline (tree learners, TF-IDF views, fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 encoders, attention classifier, LPcodedec replication), every result file behind the article's tables and figures, the Colab notebooks for the GPU baselines, and the scripts that rebuild the corpus, run every experiment and regenerate every table and figure. The human-written files come from public repositories under the MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 2-Clause and BSD 3-Clause licences and are redistributed under those licences with their notices preserved. Personal markers in identifiers were anonymised. The scripts are released under the MIT licence. The LPcode benchmark and the LPcodedec code of Park et al. are not redistributed; the README documents how to obtain them.

items.summary: This repository provides the compiled analysis inputs, R code, figure source data and GIS rasters supporting the manuscript “Historical introduction pools pre-structure future plant invasion debt under climate change”. Version 2.0 contains the final USA-intersection climatic-analogue reconstruction and its corresponding model predictions and spatial summaries. The historical introduction pool contains 18,562 species. The stage-transition models use 5,791 complete-case species, of which 4,088 species without a recorded invasion form the future candidate invasion-debt subset. Future predictions cover 12 combinations of two climate scenarios (SSP126 and SSP585), three periods (2041–2060, 2061–2080 and 2081–2100), and two global climate models (HadGEM3-GC31-LL and MPI-ESM1-2-HR). The archive contains: • Figure_data: XLSX source workbooks for main Figures 1–4, Supplementary Figures S1–S4 and Supplementary Tables S1–S15, together with the compiled species-level analysis dataset and current and future candidate-species predictions. • Code: R scripts, computational inputs and provenance documentation for the stage-transition models, climatic-analogue searches, future predictions, phylogenetic null analysis, temporal analyses, sensitivity analyses and publication source tables. • GIS_rasters: GeoTIFFs for the main and supplementary spatial figures. Main Figure 4 rasters contain sums within globally aligned 0.5° display cells; supplementary spatial rasters retain the native 10-arc-minute resolution. • Validation: execution records and numerical checks. • README files: instructions for reproducing the analyses, plotting the source data and interpreting the spatial fields. Current and future closest US climatic analogue cells are identified separately for each candidate species. POT is the sum of future predicted invasion probabilities assigned to future analogue cells. CHG is future grid-level transition potential minus current grid-level transition potential, with unassigned cells completed with zero. CHG therefore incorporates both changes in predicted probability and relocation of climatic analogues. POSDP is the sum of positive species-level changes assigned to future analogue cells; Supplementary Figure S3 reports its range across the two climate models. The analytical workflow was tested with R 4.3.3. Reproduction starts from the compiled historical master dataset, supplied phylogenetic inputs, prepared species climatic centroids and extracted WorldClim grid values. The package does not independently repeat every upstream archive-curation decision, manual stage-status assignment, GBIF download or occurrence-cleaning step. These boundaries and the optional XLSX and GeoTIFF export procedures are documented in the README. The historical count of 15,950 candidate invasion-debt species is retained for historical summaries; it is not the population used for future predictions. This release supersedes the earlier spatial outputs based on a rectangular climate-search domain. Future results should be interpreted as conditional model projections rather than evidence of a statistically established climate-driven increase in invasion. items.summary: GradLint is a fast, standalone Rust-based command-line tool and Python package for diffusion MRI gradient-table quality control. It audits FSL and MRtrix gradient schemes, detects b-vector flip and axis-permutation errors using DWI image evidence, and writes corrected gradient tables with machine-readable provenance. GradLint is designed as a QC gate before diffusion MRI preprocessing, reconstruction, or tractography pipelines. It checks whether the supplied gradient table is geometrically consistent with the diffusion image, reports scheme-quality issues such as shell structure, direction counts, b0 handling, non-unit b-vectors, and angular sampling, and identifies silent convention errors that can otherwise propagate into tensor fitting and tractography results. The core detection method ranks signed axis permutations of the gradient table by a fibre-coherence criterion derived from a diffusion tensor fit. Candidate conventions are evaluated in the appropriate image or world frame for the input format: FSL bvec/bval tables are treated as image-relative, while MRtrix .b tables are treated as world-coordinate gradients. When a high-confidence correction is found, GradLint can emit repaired FSL and/or MRtrix gradient files together with JSON provenance describing the decision, transform, inputs, and outputs.  The software is implemented as a Rust core with thin command-line and Python interfaces. The Python package exposes the same functionality as the CLI and can render JSON reports to Markdown or HTML. Input gradient files are never modified in place unless an explicit overwrite option is used. This record archives the source code for GradLint v1.1.6, corresponding to the GitHub release published on 2026-10-03. The archived source includes the Rust core, CLI, Python bindings, report rendering layer, tests, CI/release metadata, and example materials included in the public source tree. items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. items.summary: Classical metaphysics treats the mutual exclusivity of alternatives as primitive: or, in its physical reading, excludes by nature. This paper argues the polarity should be reversed. Exclusivity is an achievement — stated, interior, structural content of the alternatives them-selves — rather than an intrinsic feature of disjunction; and once exclusion is relocated from the exterior of or to interior content, a new composition regime falls out with no further postulation: the joint regime, in which co-present alternatives simply decline to carry mu-tual negations. The difference between the regimes is fixed by a one-statement test, which answers the suspicion of mere notation; a strict fence separates what the new primitive sup-plies (openness) from anything its occupants might do with it (use), which blocks the two natural misreadings; and the primitive itself receives a deflationary definition: or-jointness is the logic-valued regime of not stating mutual negations on the interior side — obtained by declension, not addition. We argue the proposal reclassifies the color-exclusion problem that fractured the Tractatus, and supplies the determinable-based literature on metaphysical indeterminacy with the composition story it has lacked. A documented fact about the direction of discovery then bears on the proposal’s status: the two composition forms were first extracted, in companion work, from the case-by-case structure of interference phenomena — before the present philosophy existed — so the dichotomy’s shape is explained by what it was extracted from, not by any philosophical purpose it might serve. Whether the world instantiates the joint regime is the companion framework’s proposal, on which no thesis here leans; what the provenance establishes is that the primitive was not gerrymandered for the argument that now exposes it.
items.title: Exclusivity as Achievement: Relocating Mutual Exclusion to the Interior, and the Logical Primitive That Falls Out

items.summary: The laws of physics are CPT-symmetric, yet laboratory quantum mechanics prepares the past and only samples the future. This working paper distinguishes five levels of taking the symmetry seriously — symmetric laws with the open future left implicit, a two-boundary description, symmetric processes, a nontrivial final boundary, and laboratory access to it — places published views and experiments on them, and states what each predicts for a final-boundary test, in which an engineered terminal acts on a flag and an entangled partner is read on every trial. Exact results: an open future propagates backward through any physical channel; a terminal can only transfer, never manufacture, final-side contrast, giving lambda = tanh(hbar omega / 2 k T_f) in a swap model, the mirror of a reset; a clamp of budget A needs an energy of at least k T_f ln A in some branch; under free local control any every-trial final condition signals, with visibility equal to the clamp strength. Under stated transfer models a null reads as a lower bound on a swap-equivalent final temperature (Partridge: above 3.5e7 K for escaping microwaves; planned qubit tests: about 27 K and 360 K). The paper audits transport to the future, specifies what any physical source of a final condition must supply, and finds that no named candidate meets the specification. CPT motivates the reversed-resource question; channel duality bounds its possible transfer; laboratory access remains an additional physical hypothesis, decided only by experiment. No new experimental result is reported. Drafted with AI assistance and revised after AI-assisted reviews; responsibility rests with the author.

items.summary: This chapter develops the research programme of Generative Relational Economics (GRE) by translating the conceptual, methodological, and substantive architectures developed earlier in the book into a cumulative, contestable, and revisable programme of inquiry. Its principal concern is answerability: GRE claims should specify what is being investigated, what kinds of evidence can support them, what would count against them, which methods are appropriate to their objects, and under what conditions their scope, formulation, or status should change. The chapter first distinguishes the epistemic status of GRE claims and establishes a modular research architecture. It then formulates research programmes for relational economic structures, allocation, heterogeneous value, value conversion and circulation, generative return, generative spacetime, fast–slow dynamics, economic power, justice, generative exploitation, epistemic economy, and AI-mediated capability asymmetry. These substantive programmes are complemented by domain studies, formal modelling, historical and interpretive inquiry, quantitative and empirical research, comparative theory, institutional experimentation, measurement analysis, counterevidence, negative results, replication, reinterpretation, and research infrastructure. A recurring concern is to prevent operationalization from collapsing the distinctions that motivate GRE. Measurement is therefore treated as a transformation with possible loss and reflexive effects; formalization is treated as task-relative rather than as evidence of ontological commitment; justice research keeps normative premises explicit; power and exploitation require mechanism-level identification rather than inference from asymmetry alone; and cross-domain translation preserves non-equivalence and domain-specific remainders. Failed models, failed translations, null results, counterexamples, and negative evidence are treated as constitutive resources for cumulative research rather than as residuals to be discarded. The chapter concludes by specifying how GRE may interact with neighboring Generative Relational domains while retaining disciplinary containment. Candidate cross-domain structures remain hypotheses for further inquiry rather than presumptive components of a completed general theory. GRE thereby emerges not as a closed theoretical system, but as an open research programme whose concepts, methods, models, and domain claims remain historically situated, empirically answerable, formally inspectable, and institutionally revisable.

We settle an open problem about such layers and then identify what actually governs them. items.summary: Sunnycode v1 provides an open-access computational framework and reproducibility package supporting the research article Failure-Aware Gateway Placement and Road-Constrained Backbone Optimization for Resilient Urban LoRaWAN Networks , submitted to Digital Communications and Networks. The framework integrates OpenStreetMap (OSM) building-level sensing demand, radio-frequency (RF) feasibility, capacity-aware gateway assignment, worst-case single-gateway failure retention (N−1), gateway-load fairness, and road-constrained Steiner backbone synthesis. The repository includes Python implementations of the proposed optimization approach and four independent benchmark methods (Genetic Algorithm, Particle Swarm Optimization, Greedy, and Random Search). Dataset and experimental scope The computational experiment considers 685 building-level sensor anchors, 169 road vertices, 195 street edges, and 89 gateway candidates. The Full benchmark comprises 4,000 run-level observations obtained from 100 repetitions for each combination of five optimization methods and eight gateway budgets (k = 3–10). Repository contents Python source code and computational validation utilities. Nine original CSV files containing experimental observations, aggregated statistics, evaluation effort, and optimizer provenance. OpenStreetMap territorial input ( sunny3.osm ). Forty scientific figures in PDF format. Installation and execution instructions using Anaconda. SHA-256 file-integrity manifest and licensing information. The archived results support independent verification of the reported statistics and new computational experiments. The original historical environment metadata and detailed event histories are not included; therefore, bit-for-bit replay of the historical execution environment is not claimed. Scientific scope: RF coverage and packet delivery ratio are model-derived planning estimates rather than field-calibrated measurements. N−1 resilience represents gateway-access service retention and does not certify fault-tolerant physical-backbone connectivity. This software and dataset are released to support transparent computational research, independent assessment, and further development of resilient urban Internet of Things infrastructure planning.

items.summary: This repository provides the code, fitted probe weights, steering vectors, and experimental records for SelfHalt: Auditing Activation Steering for LLM Reasoning-Length Control . items.summary: This Zenodo record is a permanently preserved version of a PREreview. You can view the complete PREreview at https://prereview.org/reviews/23147092 . ## Summary This paper identifies a genuinely under-appreciated routing axis: after a model router picks Llama-3.3-70B, the client must still choose *which provider serves it* — and the price list is a bad guide. Measuring live endpoints across 6 open models, multiple providers, and three waves over 43 days, the authors find price predicts latency (median Spearman −0.61) but not accuracy (+0.05) or availability (0.00); feasibility is task-selective (one Llama-3.3-70B deployment is near-normal on knowledge tasks but catastrophically degraded on multi-step reasoning); and the map drifts (routes changed in 4/17 comparable cells over days 0–13). Their measured-map policy — cheapest provider within 5 points of best measured accuracy with >90% availability — yields median 50% savings vs. the premium provider at matched quality. FACET, their online router, certifies per-(provider×task) feasibility facets before serving cheap endpoints, fails safe to an anchor, and monitors certified facets with a slip detector. A 36-hour live run (Llama-3.3-70B, 12 providers, 538 queries) cut average served price from $0.924/M to $0.210/M tokens — 63.7% serving-cost reduction (57.1% incl. probes) at 88.3% accuracy. ## Strengths 1. **The decision axis is real and well-positioned.** Same weights, different quantization/kernels/batching, wildly different service — anyone running multi-provider open-weight inference has felt this. Appendix B's Table 7 draws the line cleanly against FrugalGPT/RouteLLM/CARROT/MixLLM: those pick the model; this picks the server underneath, and the two layers compose (Section 5). 2. **Unusually honest measurement reporting.** Three-wave drift study, thorough Appendix A limitations (attribution-agnostic claims; pinned probing can induce rate limits; single aggregator and client location; price–latency is associational, not causal). The task-selective failure finding alone is worth the paper. 3. **FACET is framed as insurance, not optimization.** Separating certification (admission) from monitoring (drift) with component ablations (Tables 3–4), plus an explicit break-even analysis of the safety premium (~17× an ordinary query vs. SW-UCB, Appendix E), is the right framing: you pay for the anchor to avoid serving a catastrophic mine. ## Major concerns 1. **The live deployment never tests the core mechanism.** The single 36-hour run is caveated: "no provider quality collapse occurred during this window, so the experiment validates cold-start certification and live migration rather than slip detection." Slip detection is FACET's raison d'être, and it is exercised only in exact-replay — with Appendix A admitting the ablation and bias stress tests all use a single Llama-3.3-70B/GSM8K replay cell. The headline experiment should show the detector catching a real slip, on multiple cells, live. 2. **Threshold fragility is buried in the appendices.** The 50% saving rests on δ=0.05, nmin=12, 90% availability — but the out-of-sample below-floor rate swings from 0% to 22.2% across threshold choices (Appendix H), and the confidence-based analysis cuts median savings from 55% to 46% (Appendix U). The main text should carry uncertainty-quantified savings, not point-estimate victory margins. 3. **The trust boundary reintroduces the cost the paper claims to remove.** Systematic evaluator bias "can corrupt certification unless ground-truth probes or audits provide an independent quality signal" — but ground-truth labels for arbitrary production queries are exactly what doesn't exist. And the anchor must be maintained: in practice it's the premium provider you were trying to escape. Who pays for the anchor and the gold audits is left unquantified. ## Practitioner perspective The task-selective failure finding is the one I'd pin to every team's wall: provider safety is a (provider × task × time) mea

items.summary: Abstract   The Universal Research System with Reverse Itinerary (SUII) is a retrospective analytical methodology designed to reconstruct, in a traceable and auditable manner, the probable pathway leading from an initial problem or question to a completed scientific product. This manual brings together the universal prompt, a mandatory common core, ten core modules—including bibliographic analysis (SUII-B)—and six specialised extensions: journalistic and opinion texts (SUII-P), audiovisual or audio documents (SUII-AV), legislation and regulatory documents (SUII-L), case law and judicial decisions (SUII-J), critical appraisal of scientific articles (SUII-LC), and traceable research information management for datasets and research data objects (SUII-TRIM). Each module guides the extraction of locatable traces, classification of the epistemic status of claims, and construction of matrices linking evidence, inference, confidence, alternatives, and required verification. SUII-TRIM extends this logic to the provenance, versioning, transformation, quality control, preservation, access, and reuse of research datasets, while preserving the distinction between directly observed information, information provided by the researcher, reasoned inference, and non-determinable information. The method separates retrospective reconstruction from the prospective generation of hypotheses and requires rival explanations whenever the evidence does not support a unique conclusion. It also incorporates procedures for methodological auditing, version comparison, conceptual genealogy, peer review, algorithmic-bias assessment, external validation, teaching, and traceable research data management. SUII is not intended to recover the authors’ actual psychological history or to replace validated tools for methodological appraisal, risk-of-bias assessment, certainty of evidence, data stewardship, or repository curation. Its application requires version-controlled corpora, decision logs, retention of prompts and outputs, source verification, preservation of original data objects when applicable, and mandatory human oversight. When the available traces are insufficient, the appropriate result is “not determinable.” The manual provides practical criteria for selecting, combining, and quality-controlling the modules according to the product under analysis and the research objective, while maintaining explicit boundaries between documented evidence, reasoned inference, speculation, and unresolved uncertainty .   Resumen   El Sistema Universal de Investigación con Itinerario Inverso (SUII) es una metodología de análisis retrospectivo orientada a reconstruir, de forma trazable y auditable, el itinerario probable que conduce desde un problema o pregunta inicial hasta un producto científico finalizado. Este manual reúne el prompt universal, un núcleo común obligatorio, diez módulos nucleares y seis extensiones especializadas: análisis bibliográfico (SUII-B), textos periodísticos y de opinión (SUII-P), documentos audiovisuales o sonoros (SUII-AV), legislación y normativa (SUII-L), jurisprudencia y sentencias (SUII-J), lectura crítica de artículos científicos (SUII-LC) y gestión trazable de información y datos de investigación (SUII-TRIM). items.summary: Replication package for the journal article on attributing LLM-paraphrased source code to the model that produced it, in the setting where someone has an LLM rewrite code that another person wrote so that it no longer looks copied. Contents: the corpus of 144,958 paraphrase pairs (22,053 human-written files in Python, C, C++, Java, C#, Go and PHP, rewritten by Gemini 3 Flash, GPT 5 Nano, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen 3 Coder 30B, DeepSeek V3.2, Grok 4 Fast and Devstral 2512 under the paraphrasing instruction of Park et al., 2025), the deterministic fold assignment, the 105-feature matrix, the cross-prompt corpus (the same 1,050 files rewritten under two further instructions), 2,400 human revisions of source files from MIT-licensed repositories (the negative set of the paired detection experiment), the out-of-fold outputs of every view and baseline (tree learners, TF-IDF views, fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 encoders, attention classifier, LPcodedec replication), every result file behind the article's tables and figures, the Colab notebooks for the GPU baselines, and the scripts that rebuild the corpus, run every experiment and regenerate every table and figure. The human-written files come from public repositories under the MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 2-Clause and BSD 3-Clause licences and are redistributed under those licences with their notices preserved. Personal markers in identifiers were anonymised. The scripts are released under the MIT licence. The LPcode benchmark and the LPcodedec code of Park et al. are not redistributed; the README documents how to obtain them.

items.summary: The Olist Transactional Evidence Benchmark (OTEB) is a neutral, derived research dataset for evaluating analytical methods under incomplete, conflicting, ambiguous, and reconstructable transactional evidence. OTEB is derived from the Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist . It provides a frozen reference cohort of 94,791 internally reconciled orders, 901 deterministic controlled instances, transaction-instance membership, evaluator-only oracle states, and state-specific monetary exposure. The benchmark represents four evidence states: `CONFIRMED`, `RECONSTRUCTED`, `CONFLICTING`, and `UNRESOLVED`. Controlled families cover missing evidence, hard conflicts, unique reconstruction, ambiguous reconstruction, duplicate evidence, and mixed corruption at 5%, 10%, 20%, 30%, and 40%. This release contains the reference oracle, controlled-instance definitions, compact membership index, exposure tables, data dictionary, provenance documentation, reconstruction code, validation code, manifests, schema catalog, and checksums. It contains no method predictions, comparative performance results, ablation studies, paper drafts, dashboards, or private Rahaskin data. Raw Olist CSV files are not redistributed and must be obtained from the original Kaggle source. Original source citation: Olist, & Sionek, A. (2018). Brazilian E-Commerce Public Dataset by Olist [Data set]. Kaggle. https://doi.org/10.34740/KAGGLE/DSV/195341 Official source: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/olistbr/brazilian-ecommerce License: Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-ShareAlike 4.0 International (`CC BY-NC-SA 4.0`).

items.summary: This reproducibility package accompanies the article “Decomposing cross-study disagreement in renewable-energy priorities: a provenance-preserving typed RASS framework for Türkiye”. It contains the machine-readable source registry, source-extracted numerical tables with article-level provenance, typed records, configuration and policy files, Python analysis code, tests, computational certificates, derived outputs, and figure and table source assets supporting the reported analyses. The package supports source-native replication audits of four published Türkiye renewable-energy prioritization studies; controlled representation and operator experiments; ordinal and numerical evidence synthesis; weight–ontology–missingness robustness analyses; and theorem-certificate checks. Copyrighted publisher PDF files are not included. The source articles are identified through their bibliographic information and DOIs in the source registry. No personal or sensitive data are included. Version 1.0. Usage and reproduction instructions are provided in README.md, and file integrity information is provided in SHA256SUMS.txt.
items.title: Reproducibility data and code for Decomposing cross-study disagreement in renewable-energy priorities: a provenance-preserving typed RASS framework for Türkiye

items.summary: Replication package for the journal article on attributing LLM-paraphrased source code to the model that produced it, in the setting where someone has an LLM rewrite code that another person wrote so that it no longer looks copied. Contents: the corpus of 144,958 paraphrase pairs (22,053 human-written files in Python, C, C++, Java, C#, Go and PHP, rewritten by Gemini 3 Flash, GPT 5 Nano, Claude 3 Haiku, Qwen 3 Coder 30B, DeepSeek V3.2, Grok 4 Fast and Devstral 2512 under the paraphrasing instruction of Park et al., 2025), the deterministic fold assignment, the 105-feature matrix, the cross-prompt corpus (the same 1,050 files rewritten under two further instructions), 2,400 human revisions of source files from MIT-licensed repositories (the negative set of the paired detection experiment), the out-of-fold outputs of every view and baseline (tree learners, TF-IDF views, fine-tuned CodeBERT and CodeT5 encoders, attention classifier, LPcodedec replication), every result file behind the article's tables and figures, the Colab notebooks for the GPU baselines, and the scripts that rebuild the corpus, run every experiment and regenerate every table and figure. The human-written files come from public repositories under the MIT, Apache 2.0, BSD 2-Clause and BSD 3-Clause licences and are redistributed under those licences with their notices preserved. Personal markers in identifiers were anonymised. The scripts are released under the MIT licence. The LPcode benchmark and the LPcodedec code of Park et al. are not redistributed; the README documents how to obtain them.

items.summary: CORE-LLM-Bench is a controlled neurosymbolic benchmark for evaluating ontology-grounded reasoning in large language models. Version 1.1.0 contains 9,048 unique question-hop instances derived from four ontology datasets: Family, Pizza 100, Pizza 250, and OWL2Bench. The benchmark contains 6,032 binary question-answering (BQA) instances and 3,016 open-ended question-answering (OEQA) instances. Benchmark instances support 1-hop and 2-hop ontology contexts and aligned natural-language (NL), formal-symbolic (FS), and entity-abstracted (AR) representations. Ground-truth answers and explanation structures are derived using symbolic ontology reasoning, enabling controlled evaluation according to task formulation, representation, semantic abstraction, context depth, explanation-based reasoning complexity, and reasoning type. The release includes benchmark data, reasoning metadata, provenance and licensing documentation, release manifests and checksums, and scripts supporting benchmark generation, validation, Hugging Face export, and reproducibility. The canonical source-code release is CORE-LLM-Bench v1.1.0 on GitHub. Licensing is component-specific. Repository software is MIT licensed; separable original CORE-LLM-Bench benchmark content is CC BY 4.0; Pizza-derived material follows CC BY 3.0; OWL2Bench-derived material follows Apache-2.0; and Family/FHKB-derived material follows CC BY-SA 3.0. See NOTICE.md for detailed provenance, attribution, and modification information.
items.title: CORE-LLM-Bench: A Controlled Neurosymbolic Benchmark for Ontology-Grounded Reasoning in Large Language Models
